E.title: Listening 1 — A Student Podcast on Digital Responsibility
E.passage:
Layla: Welcome to Smart Choices. Today Yousuf is telling us about an online exhibition his class created. What was the exhibition about?
Yousuf: We collected photographs of traditional crafts in our town, but wanted to tell the stories behind them rather than simply post pictures.
Layla: How did the class find reliable information?
Yousuf: First, we interviewed local artists with their permission. Then we checked dates and descriptions with a museum guide. One online caption gave the wrong name for a tool, so we corrected it before publishing.
Layla: Did everyone agree to show their face?
Yousuf: No. Two artists preferred to show only their hands at work. We respected their choice and used photographs of the objects instead.
Layla: How did you make the exhibition accessible?
Yousuf: We recorded short audio descriptions in both English and Arabic, with clear titles for younger visitors.
Layla: What technical problem did the team face?
Yousuf: Our first website loaded slowly on mobile phones. We reduced the image sizes and tested the pages on different devices before inviting families.
Layla: What will happen next?
Yousuf: The class will ask visitors for suggestions. We hope to create another section about traditional musical instruments next term.

F.title: Listening 1 — Preserving a Traditional Falaj
F.passage:
Amina: Our school heritage club is visiting an old falaj this week. Hamed, you recently joined a team studying its water channel. What surprised you?
Hamed: I had seen the small stream beside the palm gardens, but I had never realised how carefully people managed the flow of water.
Amina: How does the falaj help farms?
Hamed: Water travels along channels towards different gardens. Traditionally, farmers followed a shared timetable so families knew when water would reach their land.
Amina: What did your team do during the first visit?
Hamed: We walked with a local guide, sketched the channel and photographed a stone marker. The guide asked us not to enter narrow sections because the ground could be slippery.
Amina: Did you repair anything yourselves?
Hamed: No. Repairs need trained people. Instead, we collected information and removed a few empty bottles from a safe public path.
Amina: What problem did the guide describe?
Hamed: Some visitors leave rubbish near the channel, and others step over old walls to take photographs. Both actions may damage the site.
Amina: How will you share what you learnt?
Hamed: We are preparing a simple visitor map and a short bilingual presentation for the school assembly.
Amina: What should visitors remember?
Hamed: Stay on marked paths, follow the guide's instructions and respect the families who still use the water system.
